verdict.rationale: Otter documents a Public API and webhooks (listed on the pricing page) and an official OAuth-secured MCP server, but these are described mainly as ways to export or connect meeting data. Searching transcripts, analyzing meetings and pushing data to other systems are covered. Nothing shows UI parity, such as scheduling the notetaker, uploading or transcribing files, managing channels, editing notes, sharing or admin settings through the API. Missing for 10: API reference documentation, evidence of write and control operations matching the UI (recording/scheduling, imports, channels, collaborative editing, admin), explicit parity claims, independent or hands-on corroboration.
